fieldMarks: Rich russet-tan coat with white underparts, large white rump patch and two white bands across the throat.
Bucks have 13–16 in horns with a forward prong and curved tips, plus black cheek patches and snout band; about 70% of does have short (about 1.5 in) horns.
Both sexes shed the horn sheaths every year.
behavior: Relies on keen eyesight and rapid flight; alarmed animals snort, erect the white rump hair and release musk.
Bucks hold territories March–September; does travel in small herds; herds aggregate in winter.
Eats forbs in spring and summer and browse (especially big sagebrush) in winter.
Some northern herds migrate up to 200 miles a year on consistent routes; fences obstruct movement.
habitat: Open grasslands and sagebrush-grasslands on low, rolling terrain with long sight lines.
range: From southern Alberta and Saskatchewan south to northern Mexico, west to eastern Oregon and northeastern California and east to the Dakotas and Texas; largest numbers in Wyoming and Montana.
